intro: Buddhists tell hundreds of stories about the Buddha's lives before he was the Buddha. These are called Jataka tales. In many of them, he is an animal.
In this unit you will hear two of them. A Monkey King saves his friends. A hare gives the only gift he has. You will be able to retell each tale and say what it teaches.
bigQuestion: What can animal stories teach about kindness and giving?

timeline.t: Monkeys live happily in a mango tree by a river.
A human king and his archers circle the tree.
The Monkey King makes a bridge with his body.
The monkeys cross, and the human king learns about good leaders.
Four friends decide to give gifts to anyone in need.
A hungry traveler comes, and three friends find food.
The hare offers himself, and the fire feels cool.
The tale says Sakka draws the hare on the moon.

words.d: a story Buddhists tell about one of the Buddha's earlier lives
being brave when something is hard
something you can walk across to get over water
a person who helps and guides a group
a short animal story that teaches a lesson
to give some of what you have to others
to hold something out for someone to take
a king of the gods in Buddhist stories

choices: a story of the Buddha's earlier life
test.why: Buddhists tell Jatakas about the Buddha's earlier lives.

test.q: In many Jatakas, the Buddha-to-be is...
test.why: In many tales he is a monkey, a deer, a hare or another animal.

test.q: How did the Monkey King save his monkeys?
choices: made a bridge with his body
test.why: He stretched his body to finish the bridge.

test.q: What did the human king learn?
choices: a good leader cares for the group
test.why: The Monkey King taught him what a good leader does.

test.q: Who were the four friends in the Hare Jataka?
test.why: The tale names a hare, a monkey, a jackal and an otter.

test.q: Why did the hare have nothing to share?
test.why: People cannot eat grass, so the hare had no food to give.

test.q: Who was the traveler in the Hare Jataka?
test.why: The tale says the traveler was Sakka in disguise.

test.q: Where does the tale say the hare's picture is?
test.why: The tale says Sakka drew the hare on the moon.

test.q: Which is a fable from Greece?
test.why: The tortoise and the hare is one of Aesop's fables. The other two are Jatakas.

test.q: What do both tales in this unit teach?
test.why: Both tales show caring for others, a value Buddhists teach with Jatakas.

write.prompt: Pick the Monkey King or the hare. Tell what the animal did and why. Name the tale and what Buddhists say it teaches.
tips: Name the tale, like "the Hare Jataka."
Use one word from the unit, like courage or share.
